image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Multi-series line chart**

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **multiple lines in a single panel**
- No faceting or small multiples
- No stacking
- Series are distinguished primarily by **color** and **direct end labels**

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Year (2015–2022) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Average wage growth since 2015 (%) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis |
| Worker group / occupation category (Santa, Leisure & hospitality, Retail, All workers, Hospitals, Managers) | Categorical/nominal | Line color/lightness, separate line series, direct text labels at line ends |

comments.raw_comment:
1. I primarily noticed that every occupational position in the graph has an upward trend showing that wages are growing across all industries. This is extremely important to our national economy and our global community for the functioning of our human race. What I found very interesting is that jobs in the retail and leisure section saw the most wage growth over 2020-2022 when compared to other jobs such as a doctor, lawyer, or healthcare worker, which generally require thousands in student debt, those jobs saw more growth, possibly showing a higher demand for jobs in those fields. 
2. As I am a rising high school graduate, college is a main focus, and with that comes the thought of student loans and debt. What I am wondering is, how has the wage grown over the past five years compared to the student loans citizens need to take out to get into that occupational field? 
3. Within almost every community around the world, there is a socioeconomic gap or divide at some point, and this graph reflects pretty powerful information. Oftentimes jobs in retail can be not too hard in terms of entry qualifications, and this means that you may not be required to pay high levels of college debt. This is surprising as in our society today there is such high pressure on high schoolers to go into thousands of dollars of debt to get a “good” job. 
4. The occupation on the uprise

I notice that Santa’s wage grows exponentially from 2020 to 2022. It took a dip from 2019 to 2020 most likely because of Covid. I wonder how much Santa’s average wage is now. I wonder if Santa is just a crazy good businessman to have his wage grow so drastically from 2020 to 2022.

This impacts me and my community because Santa brings gifts to all the world's people on Christmas Day. He also is the centerpiece in most Christmas specials in TV and movies.

Santa’s wage goes sky-high!

What I notice:
I notice that from 2019 to 2020, Santa’s wage growth decreased; however, from 2020 to 2022, his wage growth increased. I also notice that Santa’s wage growth increased from 2021 to 2022 more than the other jobs. In 2020, the other jobs had a larger wage growth than Santa. In 2015, Santa had a larger wage growth than the other jobs. In 2019, Santa also had a bigger wage growth. 

What I wonder:
Why did Santa have a larger wage growth than the other jobs in 2015? Why did Santa have a smaller wage growth than the other jobs in 2020? What led to a decrease in Santa’s wage growth from 2019 to 2020? What led to an increase in Santa’s wage growth from 2020 to 2022? Why does Santa get paid a wage? What does he get paid for? How much does Santa get paid compared to the other jobs?

How this relates to me and my community:
This relates to my community as Santa’s wage decreased in 2020 during the COVID year. However, the graph does not show a decrease in the wages of the other jobs, they just remain constant. This further relates to my community as many children visit Santa at the mall in order to tell him what they want for Christmas. This increases Santa’s wage. This does not relate to me as I do not celebrate Christmas and have never paid Santa to tell him what I wanted for Christmas. I am overall surprised that Santa had a higher wage growth than all of the jobs from 2020 to 2022.

“Santa Steals the Show While Also Absorbing All of the Money.”

1. What do you notice?


I noticed that between 2019 and 2020, the wage for Santa had an extreme decline by about 15% which is the only decline present. I wonder if this had to do with the Covid-19 virus that started in late 2019 in some countries, and 2020 in the United States.


2. What do you wonder?


I wonder why the wage of Santa has increased so much in the past years and has surpassed all the other jobs on this graph. Is it simply because of inflation and population growth with higher demands, or is there another factor causing this increase?


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?


This impacts the community because there are a lot of people who want to meet Santas at places like malls or superstores so the demand may be going up. Their wages are increasing more than other jobs which is surprising. This impacts the community because why are Santa's wages increasing more than essential workers like hospital workers? It seems like the wages should increase more for essential jobs like health care rather than Santas so that more people will go into healthcare and help people recover from illnesses and injuries. If hospital workers aren’t being paid enough, we might not have enough doctors and that could be a danger to the community.


4. Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

“Santa’s Big Raise”

comments.raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
Santa has been increasing their worker’s wages the most since 2020 and 2022 from nearly +5% to +43% (compared to 2015). Santa’s average wage growth dipped in 2019 to 2020 from +20% to just +5% (compared to 2015). All other sections of work such as leisure and hospitality, all workers, hospitals, managers and retail all increased near linearly from 2015 to 2020 (+0% to +13%-20%) then jumped in 2020 to 2023 increasing again linearly but about +5% to +10% per year depending on section (since 2015). 


2. What do you wonder?
I wonder why wage increases didn’t dip in all the other districts in 2020 (other than Santa). Were they not as damaged by the pandemic than Santa? I also wonder what occurred in 2016 to 2017 caused Santa to slow the wage growth (since 2015). I wonder why hospitals and managers are not seeing the same job growth as the other departments. 

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
This aids our communities especially in leisure and hospitality and retail with wage growth. Santa is also paying their workers even more with a +43% average wage growth since 2015. Managers on the other hand (along with hospitals and all workers) are not seeing as much wage growth since 2015 as the other sections of work.

4. Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
Consider This Year Working for Santa! +43% Job Growth Since 2015!!!
